newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds softer, lack hard leads.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds softer, lack hard leads.

text.p: *Australian bonds remained in tight ranges during the afternoon session, hoping for a more definite lead from U.S. Treasuries after today's January CPI report.
*Local imports jump causes only a minor flutter.
Australian bonds ended softer after trading tight ranges and hoping for a more definite lead from U.S. Treasuries after today's January U.S. CPI report.
The market had a minor flutter to the downside after January merchandise imports came in much stronger than expectations, but the move was not sustained in relatively light trade.
Imports jumped six percent against expectations for just a two percent increase with a large bulk of the increase attributed to capital imports.
"Today's (imports) numbers have no policy ramifications," said John Peters, senior economist at Westpac Banking Group.

Today's release of the Westpac-Melbourne Institute leading index of inflation showed a 0.4 point fall to 4.3 percent in December, its lowest level since late 1994 and continued to suggest only very moderate inflationary pressures.
At the same time its leading index of economic activity, which indicates where activity will be in six to nine months time, fell by 0.3 points.

However, Westpac said the smoothed growth rate still grew by 2.6 percent and averaged 3.0 percent in the December quarter, well up on the 1.1 percent of the first nine months of 1996, and a growth rate not seen since the September quarter 1994.

The local market showed a mild underperformance against the dollar bloc and was unwinding an initial tightening to Canada seen prior to its Federal budget statement earlier today. The budget contained few surprises, but Canadian analysts believe the market there could make a modest rally later today.
